mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from the pre-rate hike period (p > 0.1) during confirmed high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE changes and SPX 20-day returns falls below 0.3, or returns fail to outperform a risk-free benchmark.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% suggests strengthening demand momentum that persists into the next 5-day forward window, elevating S&P 500 valuations.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth decelerates for 3 consecutive months without a corresponding rise in SPX 5-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month indicates supply-side weakness that lags in observable price effects, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite INDPRO declines meeting or exceeding the threshold in at least 70% of such events over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.4% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a protracted Fed tightening cycle, which depresses equity valuations and drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL inflation rate rises above 0.4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns show no significant negative relationship with CPIAUCSL inflation excess over 0.4% threshold (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a decline in labor force participation (HOUST) signals a tightening labor market, which can trigger a risk-off equity sell-off and negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: During confirmed tight-labor regimes, the SPX 20-day return is positively correlated with UNRATE/HOUST changes (Pearson r > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales ( proxy via GDPC1 ) above 2% growth, without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), suggest healthy demand growth that supports equity price appreciation over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2% for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2% for the same months
failure_condition: Over 10 such instances, the 5-day SPX returns show no statistically significant positive correlation with GDPC1 growth above 2% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip industrial production decline (INDPRO) of more than 2% in two consecutive months indicates persistent supply disruptions, which often precede equity market corrections and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite INDPRO declines meeting the threshold in at least 60% of historical analogs.
